candidate_filtering_results.criterion: For untwisted D(G), invertible simples are (z,chi) with z in Z(G) and chi in Hom(G,C*), and theta_(z,chi)=chi(z). The ordinary split character test can be nonbaseline exactly when some central element survives in G_ab, equivalently the natural map Z(G)->G_ab is nonzero.
candidate_filtering_results.important_correction: Z(A4) is trivial, while A4_ab is Z/3. The Z/3 directions used by D(A4) are pure charges, hence bosonic with twist 1.

candidate_filtering_results.interpretation: This refutes the naive guess that every D(G) is split-test useless. However the signal is still only a pointed metric-group phase, not a non-pointed F/R effect.

summary.group: Dic_3, the order-12 dicyclic / binary-dihedral group Q12

candidate_filtering_results.interpretation: SU(3)_2 gives a clean simple-current phase on the ordinary separated presentation. It is a useful future candidate only after building/importing actual SU(3)_2 F/R data for the non-separated Yasui link.

separated_character_twist_reduction.consequence: On the ordinary separated presentation, F-symbols, R-symbols, fusion multiplicities, and non-pointed simple objects disappear except through the baseline Gauss sums. Therefore this cheap test filters pointed/simple-current phases, not genuinely non-pointed exotic information.
separated_character_twist_reduction.main_formula: For ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar with framings (+1,-1,-1), a universal-character assignment represented by invertibles g_h, g_e1, g_e2 has ratio theta(g_h)^-1 theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2) relative to the untwisted split value.
not_yet_proved: A fully cited theorem-level writeup for arbitrary non-separated surgery links.
A formal convention comparison for every premodular/nonmodular Yetter twist setting.
A classification statement for all U_q(g) simple-current groups and all twisted doubles D^omega(G).
proof_draft_content: For a modular category, a universal grading character is represented by an invertible simple object g via monodromy.
The +1 Gauss sum obeys tau_+(g)=theta_g^-1 tau_+(1) by reindexing X -> g tensor X.
The -1 Gauss sum obeys tau_-(g)=theta_g tau_-(1) in the unitary/ribbon setting.
The split unlink factorizes over components, so only the pointed/invertible quadratic form remains.

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit is the main D(A4)c3w1 Yasui a=1 component-A character-twist computation. It records the full 2744-sector aggregate for C=D(A4)c3w1, Link=Yasui Figure 3 a=1 R1-normalized, Yetter twist=none, and a Z/3 generator character twist on component A. The aggregate result is status pass, sector_total_present 2744, error_count 0, raw aggregate approximately 1728, and normalized value approximately 12.
commit_search_summaries.paragraph_2: For future provenance search, the commit does preserve useful performance shape: per-sector elapsed_seconds, fixed labels, hostname, worker_id, and contribution are present in the aggregate rows. The lightest recorded row is sector 0 at about 0.0000735 seconds, and the heaviest aggregate row is sector 2098 at about 279.609 seconds; summed per-row elapsed time is about 101291.36 seconds. However, the aggregate utc_start/utc_finish are only the aggregation script's 0.31 second run, not the full distributed compute window, and complete remote runtime environments are not tracked for every sector.
commit_search_summaries.subject: 收錄 Yasui a1 的 D(A4)c3w1 A 分量 twist 結果

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit records the ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar split-unlink character scan for D(A4)c3w1. It scans the Z/3^3 character assignments on the split presentation and finds no nonbaseline value: all 27 rows remain at raw value 1728 within tolerance. This is the direct split-side comparison for the component-twist experiment.
commit_search_summaries.paragraph_2: The useful future-search message is that D(A4)c3w1 does not produce a cheap ordinary-side phase in the separated presentation. The commit also includes the reproduction script da4_c3w1_split_unlink_character_scan.py, so future agents can regenerate this small scan quickly and compare it to the larger non-separated Yasui run.
commit_search_summaries.subject: 收錄 D(A4)c3w1 的 separated character scan

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit is a small candidate-screening scan on the ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar presentation. It compares four candidate categories and finds that only the pointed Vec_Z3 toy candidate has a nonbaseline separated character value; D(A4) omega0, D(A4)c3w1, and SU(3)_3 are baseline in this cheap test.
commit_search_summaries.paragraph_2: The clean takeaway is that the separated presentation is useful as a quick filter but mostly sees pointed/simple-current information. A future search for candidate filtering should find this commit before launching expensive Yasui braid computations, because it records which candidates are immediately boring on the ordinary separated side.
commit_search_summaries.subject: 收錄 CP2#2CPbar 的 separated 候選掃描

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit records the symbolic reduction for universal-character twists on ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar. The key formula is that for framings (+1,-1,-1), the character-twisted split value differs from the untwisted value by theta(g_h)^-1 theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2), where the character assignment is represented by invertible objects.
commit_search_summaries.paragraph_2: Its search value is conceptual: it explains why F-symbols, R-symbols, fusion multiplicities, and non-pointed simple objects disappear from the ordinary split-link test. It is explicitly marked INFERENCE and does not evaluate the non-separated Yasui braid presentation.
commit_search_summaries.subject: 記錄 separated character twist 的符號化化簡

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit turns the symbolic reduction into a proof-draft artifact. It states that, for an ordinary separated +/-1-framed unlink and universal-character twists, the value depends only on the pointed modular subcategory generated by invertible objects. It also lists several things not yet proved, including non-separated surgery links and convention matching for all Yetter settings.
commit_search_summaries.paragraph_2: Important caveat: this proof draft should be treated as agent-generated mathematical intuition, not as checked mathematics. It has not yet been independently verified, cited against literature, or mechanically checked. Future agents should not quote it as a theorem until it receives a separate source-audited proof note.
commit_search_summaries.subject: 保存 separated twist 只看 pointed 部分的 proof draft

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit records a proof-draft criterion for untwisted Drinfeld doubles D(G) on the ordinary separated split test. Invertible simples are pairs (z, chi) with z in Z(G) and chi a linear character, and their twist is chi(z). The split test can be nonbaseline precisely when a central element survives in the abelianization and is seen by a linear character.
commit_search_summaries.paragraph_2: The commit also fixes an important earlier confusion: Z(A4) is trivial, while A4_ab is Z/3. Thus the Z/3 direction in D(A4) is pure charge and bosonic for this split test. This commit is good search material for deciding whether a D(G) candidate is worth even a cheap separated scan.
commit_search_summaries.subject: 記錄 untwisted D(G) 的 split character criterion

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit records the D(Dic_3) ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar character scan. Dic_3 is the order-12 dicyclic or binary-dihedral group Q12; its untwisted double has simple_count 32 and global_dimension 144. The scan has status pass and finds 32 nonbaseline rows.
commit_search_summaries.paragraph_2: The clean takeaway is that not every D(G) is useless for the separated split test. D(Dic_3) gives a real pointed metric phase, though it still does not demonstrate non-pointed F/R effects or Yasui exotic separation. It is one of the two best next candidates once F/R data can be produced carefully.
commit_search_summaries.subject: 收錄 D(Dic3) 的 separated split 反例

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit records the SU(3)_2 ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar character Gauss scan. SU(3)_2 has rank 6 and a Z/3 simple-current group generated by (2,0), with generator twist exp(4*pi*i/3). The scan has status pass and finds 18 nonbaseline rows among 27 assignments.
commit_search_summaries.paragraph_2: The search value is that SU(3)_2 is a clean quantum-group counterexample to the overstrong guess that all U_q(g)-type examples are split-test trivial. But this is only a simple-current separated-side phase; real Yasui work requires producing reliable SU(3)_2 F/R symbols and checking basic links first.
commit_search_summaries.subject: 收錄 SU(3)_2 的 separated simple-current phase

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit records the SU(2)_k ordinary separated character scan through k=64. The clean rule found is that levels k congruent 0 mod 4 are baseline for every assignment in this split test, while all other tested levels have a simple-current phase.
commit_search_summaries.paragraph_2: This is a structural filter for SU(2)_k, not a positive Yasui result. It tells future searches that the separated presentation only sees the SU(2)_k simple current and should not be mistaken for non-pointed evidence.
commit_search_summaries.subject: 收錄 SU(2)_k 的 separated mod 4 掃描

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit records a non-separated Yasui a=1 SU(2)_8 all-alpha raw comparison. The artifact has status pass, elapsed_seconds about 88.66, and max_abs_difference about 1.32e-12 against the comparison target.
commit_search_summaries.paragraph_2: Its search value is negative evidence for the SU(2) route in this Yasui a=1 case. Even though separated SU(2)_k can show simple-current phases away from k divisible by 4, this saved Yasui comparison did not produce a Yasui-versus-standard discrepancy.
commit_search_summaries.subject: 保存 Yasui a1 的 SU(2)_8 all-alpha 對照

commit_search_summaries.paragraph_1: This commit creates the distilled CTL objective lab-note preimage for the Yasui a=1 character-twist work. why_some_sectors_are_easy.explanation: Some fixed-label sectors are easy because their labels force small or sparse fusion spaces along the braid word, sometimes with unit-like or low-dimensional simple objects and many zero/nonadmissible intermediate channels. working_understanding.discussion_summary_zh_hant: 我們剛剛差點把兩個圖混在一起。若一個 closed 4-manifold 沒有 1-handles、也沒有 3-handles，平常給出的 Kirby diagram 是 2-handles 的 attaching link，畫在最初 0-handle 的邊界 S^3 上；但照 Tham Definition 5.11 從下往上做，2-handle map 之後真正留給最後 4-handle 去 evaluate 的，並不是這條 attaching link 本身，而是 surgery 之後 boundary 裡的 belt-core / dual graph。這一度讓人以為：我們以前直接拿 Kirby link 做 RT/link evaluation，是不是少掛了一堆 meridian，所以算錯了。後來解開的方式是：我們其實應該把既有算法理解成從 upside-down / dual Kirby picture 在算。也就是說，Tham 從下往上得到的 belt-core graph，如果改從 4-handle 那一側往回看，就正是畫在原本 4-handle boundary 上的 dual Kirby link。這樣就不用在原始 attaching link 旁邊硬掛 meridian；掛 meridian 是另一種把 dual graph 留在 primal S^3 裡描述的中介做法，還會牽涉 3-dimensional surgery normalization。這個理解還只是工作性整理，尚未當作定理使用。
working_understanding.existing_evaluator_convention: Existing direct link evaluations should provisionally be read as using an upside-down / dual Kirby-link convention, not as a literal bottom-up implementation of Tham Definition 5.11.
working_understanding.special_dotted_knot_warning: If the original Kirby diagram contains special dotted knots, then under this Tham-5.11-compatible dual interpretation it is more natural to treat them as 3-handle / vacuum-projection data than as ordinary 1-handles directly consumable by the current framed-link evaluator.
working_understanding.why_prior_agreement_is_not_surprising: The observed agreement of complicated prior examples is evidence that the adopted convention is internally consistent; it should not be interpreted as a proof that primal attaching-link evaluation and literal Tham belt-core evaluation are raw-equal without dualization or surgery normalization.

conditional_mathematical_theorem.statement: Let C be a ribbon fusion category, let A be a finite subgroup of Aut_tensor(Id_C), and let Z_C(M,alpha) be the homologically twisted Yetter invariant. Let M and N be closed connected oriented smooth simply connected 4-manifolds, and let f:H2(M;Z)->H2(N;Z) be an integral intersection-form isometry. If the marked connected-sum formula holds with the chosen normalization, the stabilization scalar Z_C(S2xS2,0)/Z_C(S4,0) is nonzero, and the marked stable-realization argument applies, then Z_C(M,alpha)=Z_C(N,(f tensor id_A)(alpha)) for every alpha in H2(M;A).

A JSON event stream mode would be ideal for agents."},{"impact":"A human can see provider.mode=admitted-provider-adoption, but the top-level ctl_meta_commit still shows the old bootstrap commit, creating a momentary false alarm.","issue":"The final verify JSON reports bootstrap ctl_meta_commit separately from provider.current_ctl_meta_commit, which is easy to misread.","suggestion":"Rename the top-level field to bootstrap_ctl_meta_commit or add current_provider_commit at top level."},{"impact":"The agent had to infer that those files should be deleted from the final merge tree and replaced by the generated merge manifest.","issue":"The tool explains that incoming manifests are branch-local, but not what should happen to already-tracked incoming manifest files during the Git merge.","suggestion":"Have manifest-plan print explicit Git-resolution guidance: keep historical target manifests, remove listed branch-local incoming manifests from final tree, add generated merge manifest."}],"created_at":"2026-07-07T05:02:00Z","created_by":"actor:codex","mathematical_status":"NOT_A_MATHEMATICAL_CLAIM","note_id":"objective-note-2026-07-07-ctl-branch-store-merge-agent-feedback","overall_assessment":{"priority_request":"Make runbook usable directly from a Git conflict state with explicit roots, and ensure generated commands preserve the exact roots used for planning.","verdict":"The new tooling is a substantial safety improvement and did prevent a bad refs/main.json side-choice merge. The remaining pain is mostly agent UX around conflict-state bootstrap, command echoing, and actionable cleanup."},"related_artifacts":["ctl-dogfood/protocols/branch-store-merge-agents.org","ctl-dogfood/protocols/branch-store-merge-report-contract.org","ctl-dogfood/manifests/merge-2026-07-07-c99490bce09c44c5.json"],"schema":"twisted-yetter/objective-lab-note/1","scope":{"claim_boundary":"This is process feedback for upstream tooling. in particular the 2-handle map inserts a regular-colored belt-core circle in the post-attachment boundary, and the 3-handle map is a unit/vacuum-channel projection across the 3-handle co-core."}],"status":"WORKING_UNDERSTANDING_NOT_THEOREM","title":"Tham Definition 5.11 and the dual Kirby-link evaluation convention","working_understanding":{"discussion_summary_zh_hant":"我們剛剛差點把兩個圖混在一起。若一個 closed 4-manifold 沒有 1-handles、也沒有 3-handles，平常給出的 Kirby diagram 是 2-handles 的 attaching link，畫在最初 0-handle 的邊界 S^3 上；但照 Tham Definition 5.11 從下往上做，2-handle map 之後真正留給最後 4-handle 去 evaluate 的，並不是這條 attaching link 本身，而是 surgery 之後 boundary 裡的 belt-core / dual graph。這一度讓人以為：我們以前直接拿 Kirby link 做 RT/link evaluation，是不是少掛了一堆 meridian，所以算錯了。後來解開的方式是：我們其實應該把既有算法理解成從 upside-down / dual Kirby picture 在算。也就是說，Tham 從下往上得到的 belt-core graph，如果改從 4-handle 那一側往回看，就正是畫在原本 4-handle boundary 上的 dual Kirby link。這樣就不用在原始 attaching link 旁邊硬掛 meridian；掛 meridian 是另一種把 dual graph 留在 primal S^3 裡描述的中介做法，還會牽涉 3-dimensional surgery normalization。這個理解還只是工作性整理，尚未當作定理使用。","existing_evaluator_convention":"Existing direct link evaluations should provisionally be read as using an upside-down / dual Kirby-link convention, not as a literal bottom-up implementation of Tham Definition 5.11.","special_dotted_knot_warning":"If the original Kirby diagram contains special dotted knots, then under this Tham-5.11-compatible dual interpretation it is more natural to treat them as 3-handle / vacuum-projection data than as ordinary 1-handles directly consumable by the current framed-link evaluator.","why_prior_agreement_is_not_surprising":"The observed agreement of complicated prior examples is evidence that the adopted convention is internally consistent; it should not be interpreted as a proof that primal attaching-link evaluation and literal Tham belt-core evaluation are raw-equal without dualization or surgery normalization."}}

It records the full 2744-sector aggregate for C=D(A4)c3w1, Link=Yasui Figure 3 a=1 R1-normalized, Yetter twist=none, and a Z/3 generator character twist on component A. The aggregate result is status pass, sector_total_present 2744, error_count 0, raw aggregate approximately 1728, and normalized value approximately 12.","paragraph_2":"For future provenance search, the commit does preserve useful performance shape: per-sector elapsed_seconds, fixed labels, hostname, worker_id, and contribution are present in the aggregate rows. The lightest recorded row is sector 0 at about 0.0000735 seconds, and the heaviest aggregate row is sector 2098 at about 279.609 seconds; summed per-row elapsed time is about 101291.36 seconds. However, the aggregate utc_start/utc_finish are only the aggregation script's 0.31 second run, not the full distributed compute window, and complete remote runtime environments are not tracked for every sector.","subject":"收錄 Yasui a1 的 D(A4)c3w1 A 分量 twist 結果"},{"commit":"a0796cb","paragraph_1":"This commit records the ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar split-unlink character scan for D(A4)c3w1. It scans the Z/3^3 character assignments on the split presentation and finds no nonbaseline value: all 27 rows remain at raw value 1728 within tolerance. This is the direct split-side comparison for the component-twist experiment.","paragraph_2":"The useful future-search message is that D(A4)c3w1 does not produce a cheap ordinary-side phase in the separated presentation. The commit also includes the reproduction script da4_c3w1_split_unlink_character_scan.py, so future agents can regenerate this small scan quickly and compare it to the larger non-separated Yasui run.","subject":"收錄 D(A4)c3w1 的 separated character scan"},{"commit":"c1328fd","paragraph_1":"This commit is a small candidate-screening scan on the ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar presentation. It compares four candidate categories and finds that only the pointed Vec_Z3 toy candidate has a nonbaseline separated character value; D(A4) omega0, D(A4)c3w1, and SU(3)_3 are baseline in this cheap test.","paragraph_2":"The clean takeaway is that the separated presentation is useful as a quick filter but mostly sees pointed/simple-current information. A future search for candidate filtering should find this commit before launching expensive Yasui braid computations, because it records which candidates are immediately boring on the ordinary separated side.","subject":"收錄 CP2#2CPbar 的 separated 候選掃描"},{"commit":"8c74e68","paragraph_1":"This commit records the symbolic reduction for universal-character twists on ordinary separated CP2#2CPbar. The key formula is that for framings (+1,-1,-1), the character-twisted split value differs from the untwisted value by theta(g_h)^-1 theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2), where the character assignment is represented by invertible objects.","paragraph_2":"Its search value is conceptual: it explains why F-symbols, R-symbols, fusion multiplicities, and non-pointed simple objects disappear from the ordinary split-link test. It is explicitly marked INFERENCE and does not evaluate the non-separated Yasui braid presentation.","subject":"記錄 separated character twist 的符號化化簡"},{"commit":"a5cde1c","paragraph_1":"This commit turns the symbolic reduction into a proof-draft artifact. It states that, for an ordinary separated +/-1-framed unlink and universal-character twists, the value depends only on the pointed modular subcategory generated by invertible objects. It also lists several things not yet proved, including non-separated surgery links and convention matching for all Yetter settings.","paragraph_2":"Important caveat: this proof draft should be treated as agent-generated mathematical intuition, not as checked mathematics. It has not yet been independently verified, cited against literature, or mechanically checked. Future agents should not quote it as a theorem until it receives a separate source-audited proof note.","subject":"保存 separated twist 只看 pointed 部分的 proof draft"},{"commit":"1766bc8","paragraph_1":"This commit records a proof-draft criterion for untwisted Drinfeld doubles D(G) on the ordinary separated split test. Invertible simples are pairs (z, chi) with z in Z(G) and chi a linear character, and their twist is chi(z). The split test can be nonbaseline precisely when a central element survives in the abelianization and is seen by a linear character.","paragraph_2":"The commit also fixes an important earlier confusion: Z(A4) is trivial, while A4_ab is Z/3.
